# Source-region PDF fixture

`source-region.pdf` contains only synthetic English labels, generated by
`python3 make_source_region.py` using the Python standard library and built-in
Helvetica. It contains no user corpus or bundled font file.

- Page 1: single column, several distinct lines on the same physical page.
- Page 2: another physical page.
- Page 3: disjoint left and right columns; local preview must be unavailable.
- Pages 4–7: rotation 0/90/180/270, MediaBox `[20,30,632,822]`,
  CropBox `[60,90,572,762]`, testing nonzero box origins and rotated crop bounds.

The producer uses `pdftotext -bbox-layout` without `-cropbox`; its word boxes
use the rotated MediaBox top-left convention. Rendering uses `pdftoppm
-cropbox`. The test parses the actual PDF geometry with pdfcpu and recognizes
these bytes with Poppler, rather than inventing geometry for each rotation.

OCR currently creates one record per physical text line. The ALPHA label and
following lines are separate records, not evidence of automatic multiline entry
grouping. Continuous multiple-box behavior is tested separately with synthetic
cells. `marker^2` and `water_H2O` are ASCII strings, not typographic glyph tests.
